preface.p: National Anti-Corruption Commission (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Act 2022
Includes amendments up to: Act No. 23, 2023

This is a compilation of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Act 2022 that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 July 2023 (the compilation date).
The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au). The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. For more information on any uncommenced amendments, see the Register for the compiled law.

p.b: Application, saving and transitional provisions for provisions and amendments

preface.p: If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.
For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. For more information on any modifications, see the Register for the compiled law.
If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

section.heading: Transfer of information to the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector

content.p: This section applies if the Ombudsman forms the opinion that a complaint raises:
a corruption issue that is likely to involve corrupt conduct that is serious or systemic; or
a NACC corruption issue.
The Ombudsman may:
decide to refer the information the subject of the complaint to the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector, as the case requires; and
decide:
to investigate the complaint, or to investigate the complaint further; or
not to investigate the complaint, or not to investigate the complaint further.
If the Ombudsman decides to refer the information to the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector, the Ombudsman must:
refer the information as soon as is reasonably practicable; and
include with the referral all information relevant to the corruption issue or the NACC corruption issue that is in the Ombudsman’s possession or control at the time the referral is made; and
as soon as is reasonably practicable, give the complainant written notice of the following:
that the information has been referred to the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector;
the Ombudsman’s decision on whether to investigate, or continue to investigate, the complaint; and

if the Ombudsman subsequently becomes aware of any further information that is relevant to the issue—give the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector the further information as soon as is reasonably practicable.
The Ombudsman is not required to provide information to the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector under subsection (3) if:
the Ombudsman has reasonable grounds to believe the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector is already aware of the information; or
the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner or the Inspector has advised the Ombudsman that the provision of the information is not required.

(6) For the purposes of this section, a person is at executive level, in relation to an interception agency of Western Australia, if the person occupies an office or position at an equivalent level to that of a senior executive officer (within the meaning of the Public Sector Management Act 1994 (WA)).
In this Schedule:
existing inquiry: see paragraph 2(1)(b).
existing investigation: see paragraph 2(1)(a).
instrument includes:
a contract, deed, undertaking, arrangement or agreement; and
a notice, authority, order or instruction; and
an instrument made under an Act or a regulation.
NACC corruption issue transition notice: see subitem 36(4).
new Act means the National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022.
old Act means the Law Enforcement Integrity Commissioner Act 2006, as in force immediately before the transition time.
rules means the rules made under item 57.
transition determination means, in relation to an existing investigation or an existing inquiry, a determination under subitem 3(1).
transition time means the time section 40 of the new Act (which gives the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner the power to deal with a corruption issue) commences.
Expressions used in this Schedule that are defined for the purposes of the new Act, and are used in relation to that Act, have the same meaning as in that Act.
Expressions used in this Schedule that were defined for the purposes of the old Act, and are used in relation to that Act, have the same meaning as in that Act.
For the purposes of the operation of the old Act after the transition time, as provided for by this Schedule:
the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner may exercise the powers, and perform the functions and duties, of the Integrity Commissioner; and
the Inspector may exercise the powers, and perform the functions and duties, of a special investigator; and
the old Act applies with such further modifications as are necessary for matters under the old Act to be managed by the National Anti-Corruption Commission or the Inspector, as the case requires; and
the amendments made by Part 2 of Schedule 1 are taken not to have been made.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—continuation of existing investigations and inquiries

content.p: This item applies in relation to the following:

(a) an investigation (the existing investigation) of a corruption issue by the Integrity Commissioner, whether alone or jointly with another person or persons, under Part 6 of the old Act that has been commenced but is not yet completed at the transition time;
(b) a public inquiry (the existing inquiry) by the Integrity Commissioner under Part 8 of the old Act that has been commenced but is not yet completed at the transition time.
The National Anti-Corruption Commissioner may continue to conduct the existing investigation or existing inquiry under the old Act as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Note: An effect of this subitem is that the rights and obligations of persons and agencies in relation to the investigation or inquiry are determined by the old Act.
However, subitem (2) does not apply if the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner makes a transition determination in relation to the existing investigation or existing inquiry.

(1) The National Anti-Corruption Commissioner may, by notice in writing (the transition determination), determine that the new Act applies to an existing investigation or an existing inquiry if the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner considers that:
it is more appropriate to deal with the issues the subject of the existing investigation or existing inquiry under the new Act; and
in the case of an existing investigation—the issues could involve corrupt conduct that is serious or systemic.

The National Anti-Corruption Commissioner must, as soon as reasonably practicable, give a copy of the transition determination to each head of a government agency to which the existing investigation or existing inquiry relates.
The new Act applies to the existing investigation or existing inquiry from the later of the following times:
the time the transition determination is given to the head of each government agency to which the existing investigation or existing inquiry relates;
the time specified in the transition determination.

Note: The new Act will then determine the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner’s powers, functions and duties in relation to the investigation or inquiry. Similarly, the rights and obligations of persons and agencies in relation to the investigation or inquiry will be determined by the new Act.
A transition determination is not a legislative instrument.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—investigations managed or overseen by Integrity Commissioner

content.p: This item applies if, at the transition time, any of the following investigations had been commenced but had not yet been completed:
an investigation of a corruption issue by a law enforcement agency managed by the Integrity Commissioner under subsection 61(1) of the old Act;
an investigation of a corruption issue by a law enforcement agency overseen by the Integrity Commissioner under subsection 62(1) of the old Act.
The National Anti-Corruption Commissioner may continue to manage, or oversee, the investigation under the old Act as if the old Act had not been repealed.
The law enforcement agency investigating the corruption issue must comply with any reporting obligations under the old Act.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—investigations conducted solely by law enforcement agencies

content.p: This item applies if:
the Integrity Commissioner referred a corruption issue to a law enforcement agency for investigation under subparagraph 26(1)(b)(iii) of the old Act; and
the investigation had been commenced but had not yet been completed before the transition time.
The referral is taken, after the transition time, to have been made by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner under paragraph 41(1)(c) of the new Act.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—investigation of corruption issues relating to conduct of secondees

content.p: This item applies if, immediately before the transition time:
a government agency, or an integrity agency for a State or Territory, was investigating the conduct of a secondee to a law enforcement agency; and
the investigation was being done under an arrangement made under subsection 30(1) of the old Act.
The government agency, or the integrity agency for the State or Territory, may continue to investigate the corruption issue as if the old Act had not been repealed.

hcontainer.name: part
hcontainer.heading: Corruption issues previously referred or notified

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—referral and notification of corruption issues

content.p: This item applies if, before the transition time:
a person:
had referred an allegation, or information, that raised a corruption issue to the Integrity Commissioner; or
had notified a corruption issue to the Integrity Commissioner; and
the Integrity Commissioner:
had not yet decided, under Division 2 of Part 4 of the old Act, how to deal with the corruption issue; or
had decided, under that Division, how to deal with the corruption issue, but had not yet commenced taking any action to deal with the issue.
The allegation or information is taken, or the corruption issue is taken, after the transition time, to have been referred to the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner under Part 5 of the new Act.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—protection of persons referring or notifying corruption issues

content.p: If subitem 7(1) applies in relation to a person and a referral or notification, the person is taken, after the transition time, to have made a NACC disclosure under the new Act in relation to the referral or notification.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—notices to give information or produce documents or things

content.p: This item applies in relation to any of the following:

a notice given to a person, before the transition time, by the Integrity Commissioner under subsection 75(1) of the old Act requiring the recipient of the notice to give information or to produce a document or thing with which the recipient has not yet complied;
a notation included, under subsection 77A(2) of the old Act, in such a notice prohibiting the disclosure of information.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the notice and the notation as if the old Act had not been repealed.
However, if the notice or notation relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which the new Act applies because of a transition determination, then the following apply:
the notice is taken to be a notice to produce given by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner under subsection 58(2) of the new Act;
the notation is taken to be a non-disclosure notation included in the notice to produce for the purposes of subsection 95(1) of the new Act.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—protection of persons who comply with notices and protection of witnesses etc.

content.p: This item applies if one of the following was in effect immediately before the transition time:

an arrangement under subsection 81(3) of the old Act for the protection of a person who gave information, or produced a document or thing, in response to a notice served on the person under section 75 of the old Act;
an arrangement under subsection 104A(3) of the old Act for the protection of a person mentioned in subsection 104A(2) of the old Act.
The arrangement continues in effect, after the transition time, as if it had been made under subsection 116(2) of the new Act.
This item applies in relation to any of the following:

a summons issued to a person, before the transition time, by the Integrity Commissioner under subsection 83(1) of the old Act to attend a hearing to give evidence or to produce any document or thing referred to in the summons;
a notation included, under subsection 91(2) of the old Act, in such a summons prohibiting the disclosure of information.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the summons and the notation as if the old Act had not been repealed.
However, if the summons and any notation relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which the new Act applies because of a transition determination, then the following apply:
the summons is taken to have been issued by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner under subsection 63(1) of the new Act;
the notation is taken to be a non-disclosure notation included in the summons for the purposes of subsection 95(1) of the new Act.

This item applies if the Integrity Commissioner gave a direction, under subsection 90(1) of the old Act, to a person in relation to the use or disclosure of hearing material before the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the direction as if the old Act had not been repealed.

However, if the direction relates to a hearing conducted, or to be conducted, as part of an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which the new Act applies because of a transition determination, the direction is taken to have been given by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner under subsection 100(1) of the new Act.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—applications to Court to deal with contempt

content.p: This item applies if an application made to the Federal Court or a Supreme Court under section 96B of the old Act had not been dealt with by the Court before the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the application as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Subitem (2) applies whether or not the application relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which a transition determination applies.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—directions to detain in relation to contempt

content.p: This item applies if:
a direction was given under subsection 96D(1) of the old Act to detain a person in relation to a hearing of an application under subsection 96B(1) of that Act; and
the hearing had not occurred before the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the direction as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Subitem (2) applies whether or not the direction relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which a transition determination applies.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—applications for order to deliver travel documents

content.p: This item applies if an application for an order to deliver travel documents made by the Integrity Commissioner under section 97 of the old Act had not been considered by a Judge before the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the application as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Subitem (2) applies whether or not the application relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which a transition determination applies.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—orders regarding delivery of travel documents

content.p: This item applies if:
a day specified in an order to appear before the Federal Court made under subsection 98(1) of the old Act occurs after the transition time; or

the period specified in an order to deliver travel documents made under subsection 98(4) of the old Act, or the period specified in any extension to that period made under subsection 98(5) of that Act, ends after the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the order as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Subitem (2) applies whether or not the order relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which a transition determination applies.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—applications for revocation of order to deliver travel documents

content.p: This item applies if an application for a revocation of an order made under subsection 98(6) of the old Act had not been considered by the Federal Court before the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the application as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Subitem (2) applies whether or not the application relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which a transition determination applies.
This item applies if an application for an arrest warrant made by an authorised officer under section 99 of the old Act had not been considered by a Judge before the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the application as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Subitem (2) applies whether or not the application relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which a transition determination applies.
This item applies if, before the transition time:
an arrest warrant issued under section 100 of the old Act had not been executed; or
a search warrant issued under section 109 of the old Act had not expired and had not been fully executed.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the warrant as if the old Act had not been repealed.
Subitem (2) applies whether or not the warrant relates to an existing investigation or existing inquiry to which a transition determination applies.

hcontainer.name: part
hcontainer.heading: Requirements or permissions etc. under other Acts

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—notices under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006

content.p: This item applies if:
(a) before the transition time, a notice was given under section 49 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 by:
the Integrity Commissioner; or
an investigating officer who was an Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity officer; and
the period specified in the notice for compliance with the notice ends after the transition time.
The notice has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been given by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—controlled operation authorities under the Crimes Act 1914

content.p: (1) This item applies if an authority to conduct a controlled operation granted under section 15GI of the Crimes Act 1914 by an authorising officer who was an ACLEI authorising officer was in effect immediately before the transition time.
The authority has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been granted by a NACC authorising officer in relation to a corruption investigation.

(3) To avoid doubt, a reference in this item to an authority to conduct a controlled operation includes a reference to an authority to conduct a controlled operation as varied under Part IAB of the Crimes Act 1914 before the transition time.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—integrity testing operation authorities under the Crimes Act 1914

content.p: (1) This item applies if an authority to conduct an integrity testing operation granted by one of the following under section 15JG of the Crimes Act 1914 was in effect immediately before the transition time:
the Integrity Commissioner;
an Assistant Integrity Commissioner;
an SES employee in the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity.
The authority has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been granted by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner in relation to a corruption investigation.

(3) To avoid doubt, a reference in this item to an authority to conduct an integrity testing operation includes a reference to an authority to conduct an integrity testing operation as varied under section 15JK of the Crimes Act 1914 before the transition time.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—assumed identity authorities under the Crimes Act 1914

content.p: (1) This item applies if an authority to acquire or use an assumed identity granted by the Integrity Commissioner under section 15KB of the Crimes Act 1914 was in force immediately before the transition time.
The authority has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been granted by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner.

(3) To avoid doubt, a reference in this item to an authority to acquire or use an assumed identity includes a reference to an authority to acquire or use an assumed identity as varied under section 15KE of the Crimes Act 1914 before the transition time.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—witness identity protection certificates under the Crimes Act 1914

content.p: (1) This item applies if a witness identity protection certificate given by the Integrity Commissioner under section 15ME of the Crimes Act 1914 was in effect immediately before the transition time.
The certificate has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been given by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—requests for information from cash dealers under the Financial Transaction Reports Act 1988

content.p: (1) This item applies if a request given to a cash dealer by one of the following under subsection 16(4) of the Financial Transaction Reports Act 1988 had not been complied with before the transition time:
the Integrity Commissioner;
an investigating officer who was a staff member of ACLEI.
The request has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been given by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—freezing and production orders under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002

content.p: This item applies if one of the following orders, issued by a magistrate on application by the Integrity Commissioner or an authorised officer who was a staff member of the ACLEI, was in effect immediately before the transition time:
(a) a freezing order issued under subsection 15B(1) of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002;
a production order issued under subsection 202(1) of that Act.
The order has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been issued by the magistrate on application by an authorised officer who is a staff member of the NACC.

(3) To avoid doubt, a reference in this item to a freezing order includes a reference to a freezing order as extended under section 15P of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, or as varied under section 15Q of that Act, before the transition time.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—notices to financial institutions under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002

content.p: (1) This item applies if a day specified in a notice given by the Integrity Commissioner under subsection 213(1) of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 for compliance with the notice occurs after the transition time.
The notice has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been given by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—monitoring orders under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002

content.p: This item applies if:

(a) the period during which transactions must have occurred specified in a monitoring order made by a judge of a court of a State or Territory under subsection 219(1) of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 had not ended before the transition time; and
the order was made on application by the Integrity Commissioner or an authorised officer who was a staff member of the ACLEI.
The order has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been made on application by an authorised officer who is a staff member of the NACC.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—search warrants under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002

content.p: This item applies if:
(a) a search warrant issued by a magistrate under section 225 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 had not expired and had not been fully executed before the transition time; and
the warrant had been issued on application by the Integrity Commissioner or an authorised officer who was a staff member of the ACLEI.
The warrant has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been issued by the magistrate on application by an authorised officer who is a staff member of the NACC.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—surveillance device, retrieval and computer access warrants under the Surveillance Devices Act 2004

content.p: This item applies if one of the following warrants issued by an eligible Judge or a nominated AAT member on application by a law enforcement officer of the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity was in force immediately before the transition time:
(a) a surveillance device warrant issued under subsection 16(1) of the Surveillance Devices Act 2004 (including such a warrant as extended or varied under section 19 of that Act);
a retrieval warrant issued under subsection 24(1) of that Act;
a computer access warrant issued under subsection 27C(1) of that Act (including such a warrant as extended or varied under section 27F of that Act).
The warrant has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been issued on application by a law enforcement officer who is a staff member of the NACC.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—emergency and tracking device authorisations under the Surveillance Devices Act 2004

content.p: This item applies if one of the following authorisations given by an appropriate authorising officer of the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity was in force immediately before the transition time:
(a) an emergency authorisation given under Part 3 of the Surveillance Devices Act 2004;
a tracking device authorisation given under section 39 of that Act.
The authorisation has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been given by an appropriate authorising officer of the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—warrants under the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979

content.p: This item applies if one of the following warrants issued to the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity was in force immediately before the transition time:
(a) an interception warrant issued under section 46, 46A or 48 of the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979;
a stored communications warrant issued under section 116 of that Act;
a journalist information warrant issued under section 180T of that Act.
The warrant has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been issued to the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—preservation notices under the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979

content.p: (1) This item applies if a preservation notice issued by the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity under the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979 was in force immediately before the transition time.
The notice has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been issued by the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—telecommunications data authorisations under the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979

content.p: (1) This item applies if a telecommunication data authorisation made by an authorising officer of the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity under section 178, 179, or 180 of the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979 was in force immediately before the transition time.
The authorisation has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been made by an authorising officer of the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—international production orders under the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979

content.p: (1) This item applies if an international production order issued on application by the Australian Commissioner for Law Enforcement Integrity under Schedule 1 of the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979:
was in force immediately before the transition time; or
had not been given to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order was directed before the transition time.
The order has effect, after the transition time, as if it had been issued on application by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner.
This item applies if, immediately before the transition time, any of the following investigations had been commenced but not yet completed:
an investigation of an ACLEI corruption issue by the Integrity Commissioner under Division 3 of Part 12 of the old Act;
a special investigation of an ACLEI corruption issue by a special investigator under Division 4 of Part 12 of the old Act.
The National Anti-Corruption Commissioner may continue to conduct the investigation as if the old Act had not been repealed.
The special investigator may continue to conduct the special investigation as if the old Act had not been repealed.

(4) However, the Inspector may, by notice in writing (the NACC corruption issue transition notice), determine that the new Act applies to the investigation or special investigation if the Inspector considers that:

the investigation or special investigation could involve corrupt conduct that is serious or systemic.

the Inspector must continue the conduct of the investigation or special investigation under Division 3 of Part 10 of the new Act.

the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner; and
the special investigator.

the time the NACC corruption issue transition notice is given to the National-Anti-Corruption Commissioner;
the time specified in the notice.

hcontainer.heading: Information disclosure—prevention on public interest grounds

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—Attorney-General’s certificates about release of information

content.p: This item applies if:
the Attorney-General certified, under subsection 149(1) of the old Act, that disclosure of information or the contents of a document would be contrary to the public interest; and
the certificate had not been revoked before the transition time.
The old Act continues to apply in relation to the information or contents as if the old Act had not been repealed.

This item applies if, before the transition time, the Integrity Commissioner:

had not yet prepared a report on the investigation under subsection 54(1) of the old Act.

had not yet prepared a report on the inquiry under subsection 73(1) of the old Act.

hcontainer.heading: Transitional—annual reports for financial year ended before transition time

the annual report referred to in section 201 of the old Act had not been prepared for the financial year before the transition time.

examine the report; and
report to the Parliament on any matter appearing in, or arising out of, the report.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—annual reports for financial year in which transition time occurs

content.p: This item applies:
if the transition time occurs during a financial year; and

in relation to the matters that would have been covered by the annual report referred to in section 201 of the old Act for the part of the financial year before the transition time if the old Act had not been repealed.
The first annual report prepared by the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner under section 271 of the new Act must cover those matters.
This item applies if, before the transition time, the Integrity Commissioner had started preparing a special report under section 204 of the old Act, but had not completed the report.

If the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner completes the report, the Parliamentary Joint Committee on the National Anti-Corruption Commission may:
examine the report; and
report to the Parliament on any matter appearing in, or arising out of, the report.

The old Act continues to apply, in relation to the report as if the old Act had not been repealed.

This item applies to a person whose services were, immediately before the transition time, made available to the Integrity Commissioner under section 199 of the old Act.

This item applies to a person who, immediately before the transition time, was appointed as counsel assisting the Integrity Commissioner under section 200 of the old Act.

An identity card issued to the person under section 141 of the old Act is taken, after the transition time, to be an identity card issued to the person under section 268 of the new Act.
This item applies to any proceedings:
that were pending in any court or tribunal immediately before the transition time; and
to which the Integrity Commissioner was a party.
The National Anti-Corruption Commissioner is, after the transition time, substituted for the Integrity Commissioner as a party to the proceedings.

(1) This item applies if, immediately before the transition time, a person was entitled to make an application to the Federal Court or the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) under the Administrative Decisions (Judicial Review) Act 1977 for an order of review in respect of a matter arising under the old Act.

the Integrity Commissioner;
an Assistant Integrity Commissioner;
the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—confidential information provided under old Act

the Integrity Commissioner;
a staff member of the ACLEI;
if the information was provided to a special investigator for the purposes of Division 4 of Part 12 of the old Act—the special investigator.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transitional—references to the Integrity Commissioner etc. in instruments

content.p: This item applies to an instrument if:
the instrument was in force immediately before the transition time; and
the instrument contains a reference to:
the Integrity Commissioner; or
an Assistant Integrity Commissioner; or
the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity.
The instrument has effect, after the transition time, as if:
a reference in the instrument to the Integrity Commissioner were a reference to the National Anti-Corruption Commissioner; and
a reference in the instrument to an Assistant Integrity Commissioner were a reference to a National Anti-Corruption Deputy Commissioner; and
a reference in the instrument to the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity were a reference to the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

This item does not prevent the instrument from being amended or repealed after the transition time.

hcontainer.name: part
hcontainer.heading: Transitional application of certain provisions in new Act

content.p: Section 31 of the new Act applies in relation to information given by an informant whether the information is given before, on or after the commencement of that section.

The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.

The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.

The Legislation Act 2003 authorises First Parliamentary Counsel to make editorial and presentational changes to a compiled law in preparing a compilation of the law for registration. The changes must not change the effect of the law. Editorial changes take effect from the compilation registration date.

If the compilation includes editorial changes, the endnotes include a brief outline of the changes in general terms. Full details of any changes can be obtained from the Office of Parliamentary Counsel.

A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the Legislation Act 2003.
If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.
